subject: Post-call recap: hit-rate buckets & target $/1M modeling
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: hit-rate buckets & target $/1M modeling

Hi Samir — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and three asks so we can size pricing: 

Call highlights (5 bullets):
- Primary workload: customer support assistants + returns triage; ~30–40M tokens/month expected in Q3 ramp (you mentioned seasonality).
- Key constraint: procurement is targeting an effective price in the ballpark of $80–$120 per 1M tokens for production (you said "$~100 /1M" as a rough target).
- Technical note: ~60% of requests are templated/prompts with stable prefixes (good caching opportunity).
- Product ask: ability to guarantee predictable unit economics at scale and an option for a short pilot to validate hit rates.
- Procurement timeline: evaluation and PO within ~6 weeks if numbers align.

What I’m sharing now: a starter workbook with a simple prefix/cache "staircase" model that buckets traffic (hot/warm/cold) and calculates effective $/1M given different hit-rate assumptions — attached as Lumen_prefix_cache_model_v1.xlsx.

Three quick asks from you so we can firm numbers: 
1) Confirm expected steady-state monthly token volume you want us to model (you suggested 30–40M; please confirm a single point estimate).
2) Confirm whether the ~60% templated/predictable percentage is representative (or provide a split by customer-facing vs free-text).
3) Confirm procurement target range for effective $/1M (you mentioned $80–$120; we need approval to model with $80, $100, $120 band).

Next steps: once you confirm, Ben will run a sensitivity with a staircase of hit-rate buckets and we’ll return a short one-pager with: expected overall hit-rate, effective $/1M at our hosted list price, and a recommended pilot plan.

Thanks — attaching the workbook (stub).

—Stephanie

Subject: Fwd: Re: Post-call recap: hit-rate buckets & target $/1M modeling

Forwarding Samir's numbers and my quick sensitivity notes — copied into the workbook tabs.

Quoted for context:
> On Sun, 11 Apr 2027 at 10:05 AM Samir Patel <samir@lumenretail.com> wrote:
> > Steady-state tokens: target 35,000,000 tokens/month
> > Templated share: ~55–65%
> > Procurement target: $90–110 per 1M (prefer $90)

My modeling assumptions (high level):
- Baseline hosted list price used for modeling: $1,200 per 1M tokens (this is the reference list before cache savings).
- We treat cache *hits* as fully avoiding generation cost (conservative) — i.e., a hit reduces billable token count for the request.
- We bucket traffic into a 3-step "staircase":
  * Hot (15% of requests): predictable, repeated queries — expected hit-rate 80–90%
  * Warm (35%): partially templated — expected hit-rate 30–50%
  * Cold (50%): free-text/long-tail — expected hit-rate 2–8%

Using midpoints (hot 85%, warm 40%, cold 5%) -> weighted overall hit-rate = 0.15*0.85 + 0.35*0.40 + 0.50*0.05 = 0.1275 + 0.14 + 0.025 = 0.2925 (~29.3%).

Effective unit price math (simple):
- Effective billable tokens = total_tokens * (1 - overall_hit_rate).
- Effective $/1M = baseline_list_price * (1 - overall_hit_rate).

So with baseline $1,200/1M and a ~29% hit-rate -> effective price ≈ $852/1M. If we assume Redwood's negotiated discount program (e.g., committed slab) reduces baseline to $800/1M, the same hit-rate yields effective ≈ $568/1M.

Observations and asks:
1) Samir's procurement target ($90–110/1M) is much lower than our baseline scenarios; to reach that target we would need either:
  - sustained overall hit-rate > 88% (unlikely given long-tail), or
  - very aggressive committed discounts / meta-pricing (large reserved capacity with a multi-year commit), or
  - reframe the contract to include caching as an on-prem/private deployment (different pricing model).
2) A pilot that captures real prefix hit rates across a 2-week window will be decisive — suggest sampling 1–2M tokens and instrumenting prefix-level cache metrics.
3) I'll populate the workbook with a "staircase sensitivity" sheet that shows effective $/1M across baseline list prices ($1,200, $800, $400) and hit-rate bands (20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 75%).

Action items I recommend we propose to Lumen:
- 2-week pilot: 1–2M tokens, Redwood will instrument prefix cache and return per-prefix hit-rate and latency tradeoffs.
- If pilot demonstrates >35% hit-rate and latency <150ms p90, we move to a 6–12 month reserved commitment with an agreed slab price.

I flagged the workbook with preliminary numbers (see Lumen_prefix_cache_model_v1.xlsx tab "Staircase_Sensitivity").

- Ben

Samir — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clarity on targets. Summary + proposed next steps below.

Summary (one-liner): you expect 35M tokens/month steady-state, ~60% templated prefixes, procurement prefers ~$90/1M effective.

Ben's modeling (short): with conservative hit-rate midpoints we expect ~29% overall hit-rate which would imply effective $/1M around $852 on a $1,200 list price (or $568 on a $800 baseline). That gap vs. procurement's $90 target suggests the need for either very large reserved discounts or a different commercial model.

Proposed next steps (we're flexible):
1) Execute 2-week pilot (suggested scope: 1.5M tokens) under a capped spend. Redwood will provide instrumentation for per-prefix hit-rate and latency.
2) Post-pilot deliverable: a one-page "hit-rate certificate" and updated workbook showing realistic effective $/1M bands.
3) If pilot shows >=35% hit-rate and acceptable latency, we'll present reserved-capacity options (6–12 month commit) with a workback to a target effective $/1M.

Please confirm pilot scope and a preferred start date next week. If procurement needs an initial SOW, we attached a draft SOW_draft_template.pdf for your team to review.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

—Stephanie
